articleTitle: A Real Time Recognition System for Hand Gesture Language Based on Machine Learning Using SVM Model
abstract: The act of communicating involves saying what one is thinking or feeling or sharing information. Both parties must be able to speak and understand the same language for two people to be able to communicate. People who are dumb or deaf, however, use a variety of communication methods. The inability to hear or speak is referred to as being deaf or stupid. They embrace sign language to communicate with other individuals and with ordinary citizens, but the vast majority do not give sign language the reverence that it desires. It might be challenging to communicate with a deaf or dumb person because not everyone is fluent in or understands sign language. A model based on machine learning can be created to get around this challenge. To recognize various sign language gestures and translate them into English, a model can be trained. Many people who are attempting to contact and communicate with stupid and deaf people will benefit from this. The current systems for decoding Indian sign language use machine learning techniques to recognize motions made with one or both hands even though they are not real-time. In this paper, we suggest a process for producing and using an Indian Sign Language dataset and a camera, a TensorFlow model was trained, and transfer learning was used to create a real-time Sign Language Recognition system. Despite the small dataset, the system functions.

articleTitle: Vision Encoder-Decoder Models for AI Coaching
abstract: This research paper introduces an innovative AI coaching approach by integrating vision-encoder-decoder models. The feasibility of this method is demonstrated using a Vision Transformer as the encoder and GPT-2 as the decoder, achieving seamless integration of visual input and textual interaction. Departing from conventional practices of employing distinct models for image recognition and text-based coaching, our integrated architecture directly processes input images, enabling natural question-and-answer dialogues with the AI coach. This unique strategy simplifies model architecture while enhancing the overall user experience in human-AI interactions. We showcase sample results to demonstrate the capability of the model. The results underscore the methodology's potential as a promising paradigm for creating efficient AI coach models in various domains involving visual inputs. Importantly, this potential holds true regardless of the particular visual encoder or text decoder chosen. Additionally, we conducted experiments with different sizes of GPT-2 to assess the impact on AI coach performance, providing valuable insights into the scalability and versatility of our proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Compositing Machine Design and Automation: Agricultural and Enviromental Implications
abstract: Automated composting has proven to be a vital solution for the transformation of organic waste into highquality compost, soil enrichment, and improved agricultural production. This innovation responds to the need to manage urban waste efficiently and mitigate emissions of polluting gases. The implementation of the VDI 2222 Methodology ensures a structured design in key stages, from preparation to compost collection, maximizing its efficiency and quality. The use of black box simulation modeling, backed by probability distributions and precise technology, is an advanced approach to improving the process. The combination of PID controllers and IoT technologies in the control system enables real-time monitoring and adjustment of temperature and humidity, optimizing the process and reducing the environmental footprint. In addition to improving soil quality and food production, this automation is aligned with sustainability goals. Static analysis provides crucial data for the successful design and construction of the composting machine. Efficient composting automation represents an important step towards the convergence of technology and agriculture, addressing current and future challenges in food production and environmental conservation.

articleTitle: Green Synthesis of Hydroxyapatite Powder from Eggshell Biowaste for Enhanced Mechanical and Corrosion Properties in AZ91 Alloy Composites: A Powder Metallurgy Investigation
abstract: This study presents the development of hydroxyapatite (HAp) powder synthesized from eggshell bio- waste, with a subsequent investigation into its reinforcement in AZ91 alloy using powder metallurgy. Mechanical and corrosion properties of the resulting metal matrix composites (MMCs) were evaluated. The MMCs containing 18% HAp demonstrated twice the hardness of those with 0% HAp. Moreover, the MMCs with 0% HAp displayed four times greater weight gain and three times greater weight loss in simulated marine water compared to the 18% HAp MMCs. In conclusion, HAp-reinforced AZ91 alloy composites exhibit adjustable mechanical and corrosion properties.

articleTitle: Contactless Power Transfer Systems for On-line Electric Vehicles
abstract: increasing adoption of electric vehicles, demand of efficient and convenient charging solutions has become paramount. This paper explores the advancements in without contact power transmission systems specifically designed for on-line electric vehicles, addressing, challenges associated with conventional charging methods. The proposed system leverages resonant inductive coupling and innovative magnetic field optimization techniques to enable seamless power transfer between the charging infrastructure and the moving EV. By eliminating the need for physical connectors and allowing vehicles to charge while in motion, the presented contactless power transfer system aims to enhance the practicality and user experience of electric mobility. The paper discusses key design considerations, performance metrics, and safety measures, offering insights into the potential integration of this technology into existing transportation networks. Through a comprehensive review of recent developments and experimental results, this research contributes to the evolving landscape of electric vehicle charging, presenting a promising avenue for the future of online EV transfer of power systems. This article provides an overview of the Online Electric Vehicle system, as well as a look at two contactless power transfer methods that are integrated into the OLEV system. The paper contains modelling and experimental data for both types of systems, and system prototypes have been built and rigorously tested.

articleTitle: Sustainable Solution: Solar -Powered Electric Induction Cookers for Rural Areas without Additional Costs
abstract: With this project has been designed an induction electric stove powered by a photovoltaic storage system, which will make it self-sustainable without generating additional costs in the billing of electricity consumption. This solution is aimed at families in rural areas who still continue to use traditional fuels (wood, gasoline, straw, etc.) for the preparation of their food, which over time generate serious problems in people's health due to the CO2 that is produced. The project involves the implementation of a system of photovoltaic cells at the top of the houses of which would have connections to a set of batteries that would serve as the source to the operation of an electrical induction kitchen inside the house. The project demonstrates the results focused on the generation of energy capable of supplying the operation of the kitchen and for this the Helioscope simulator was used to obtain results in the photovoltaic system. These results will be used to evaluate a government project to help people stop using traditional CO2-producing and health-harmful kitchens, so implementing self-sustainable, renewable-energy induction electric kitches is the most appropriate solution.

articleTitle: A comparative study of machine learning methods: A case study of weight and growth of livestock
abstract: The observation of daily weights and growth patterns of animals is important to detect the health and nutritional status of animals. The research investigated the usefulness of machine learning (ML) models and compared the performance of Multiple Linear Regression (MLR), Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machines (SVM) and XGBoost (XGB) algorithms to predict the daily weight and growth curves of beef cattle. The min, mean, max and SD of daily weights in kg predicted using the best performing model (XGB) were 36.71, 251.74, 493.85 and 99.51 respectively. The results suggest that ML algorithms could be used as a tool to predict weight and growth of cattle using predictors such as age, sex, and breed. The model predictions and validation statistics showed that XGB is the best ML algorithm (R2 = 0.869) for predicting cattle weight using age, sex, and breed as predictors.

articleTitle: Acoustic Measurements for Hexagonal Pipe Jet Flow
abstract: The research paper aims to understand the acoustic behavior of hexagonal pipe jet flow. The length to diameter ratio of pipe is 6. The circular equivalent diameter (D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf>) is 5 mm. The Nozzle Pressure Ratio is from 2 to 6. The emission angles (ϕ) considered are 60° and 90° measured from downstream direction (jet axis). The Sound Pressure Level (SPL) and Over All Sound Pressure Level (OASPL) are compared for the two emission angles. The 90° emission angle has more harmonic peaks comparatively. The number of screech harmonics increases as NPR increases from 4 to 6. The maximum OASPL difference among the emission angles are also made and it is found to decrease with increase in NPR. The Schlieren flow visualization is done to support the acoustic data qualitatively.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning in Customer Churn Prediction for Insurance datasets
abstract: Predicting customer attrition, a critical challenge for businesses today, presents formidable obstacles. The departure of customers directly impacts an organization's reputation, financial stability, and future growth prospects. Customer behavior can change for various reasons, including uncontrollable factors or unexpected events, leading to shifts in data patterns. This can hamper the predictive accuracy of classifiers developed using traditional supervised learning techniques, especially when they rely on passive learning methods. In response to these challenges, this paper proposes the application of reinforcement learning in the context of customer churn prediction. Specifically, it utilizes the Deep Q Network (DQN) model, tailored for learning on a dedicated customer churn dataset for classification tasks. To adapt to shifting patterns, a distinct dataset is generated using shuffle sampling based on distribution. The evaluation of classifier performance is based on four key metrics: Precision, Recall, F1 score, and Accuracy. In comparison to traditional classifiers like XGBoost, Random Forest, and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), the findings underscore DQN's superiority as an active learner. DQN demonstrates enhanced predictive capabilities, especially as the dataset size grows and evolves with the emergence of new patterns.

articleTitle: Advanced Power Control Techniques and a Homogeneous Novel Concept of AC-DC Micro Grids
abstract: This article suggests simulation-based modelling and the oversight of blended AC/DC tiny grid. The small-scale grid design optimizes the electrical system's connections to variable regeneration AC and DC sources or loads by removing several reverse switches from a single AC or DC grid. Digi employed power electronic converters to connect to the grid or utility, raising questions about the devices' security and protection. It is possible to evaluate the dual AC/DC micro-grid system's performance in both grid-tied and autonomous modes. Micro grids are constructed using solar energy systems, turbine generators, and batteries. Both the DC and AC sub-grids are in synchrony, and converters are utilized for careful power transmission through the control mechanism. In a MATLAB /SIMULINK environment, the system operates.

articleTitle: Design of a Nutrient Spray System Using the ESP32 Microcontroller for Cultivation in an Aeroponic System
abstract: This study aims to implement an automation system in an aeroponic environment to improve efficiency in food cultivation. The approach is based on the use of an ESP32 microcontroller to precisely control the supply of water, nutrients and environmental conditions. Plant roots are suspended in the air and nutrients are periodically applied by spraying. The automated system monitors and controls water level, pH and electrical conductivity, ensuring optimal growing conditions without the need for constant supervision. The results show that this automation is effective in optimizing plant growth, notably increasing productivity and efficiency compared to traditional methods. In summary, this study presents an advanced and efficient solution for agriculture, taking advantage of technology. The automation system in the aeroponic environment, managed by the ESP32 microcontroller, represents an effective alternative to conventional agriculture, allowing for more efficient and productive cultivation by guaranteeing ideal growing conditions. This paves the way for the future of technologically advanced agriculture.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Solar Panel Along with Comparative Analysis of MPPT Algorithms
abstract: The renewable energy sector in India is growing very fast and the dependence on electricity generation has increased a lot compared to the last decade. As India is growing in the renewable energy sector, it is very important to understand the external variations in PV systems due to some atmospheric parameters. Much work has been done in this area, but there is still a need for research on temperature changes, the effect of shade and the effect of wind on power generation in photovoltaic systems. In the proposed method, a comparative analysis of two different maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithms is performed, and the best method is determined based on the experimental results. This article also aims to review the different literature provided in the same field in different fields of work. Several international works have been evaluated and compared with the proposed methods to get a clear idea of the shading effect on solar panels with both algorithms. The work was carried out with the aim of designing a model of a solar cell in MATLAB and therefore a PV array, which is a series combination of several solar cells. The output of the solar cell is fed to a boost converter that uses two different MPPT algorithms. The perturb-and-observe algorithm and incremental conductivity are used in this Simulink model. This model has been tested for various conditions such as light intensity change, temperature change and load resistance change. A comparative analysis is done for these changes and different courses are recorded to understand the effects.

articleTitle: Mechatronic System for Tocosh Fermentation: Design, Automation and Quality Improvement
abstract: This research presents a comprehensive approach to the design, control, and structure of an innovative fermentation machine for the production of Tocosh from potato fermentation. In order to achieve this objective, a thorough analysis of the various crucial parameters involved in the fermentation process has been carried out. The main objective of the design proposal is the real-time monitoring of essential factors such as pH and temperature in the process. To achieve this, a control system has been designed that will allow precise and constant monitoring of the temperature and pH parameters, and monitoring of the water level was also carried out to improve the quality of the product. Furthermore, the structural analysis of the fermentation chamber is addressed in detail, using Inventor software for the creation of three-dimensional models of each component and for the generation of the final design. It was revealed that the current fermentation process is based on empirical methods, involving the exposure of potatoes in areas close to lagoons or rivers for a period of between 4 and 24 months. This process lacks adequate control over the fundamental factors for successful fermentation, such as pH and temperature. Through this preliminary analysis, essential data has been collected to support the design and implementation of an innovative prototype fermentation chamber. The present study represents a significant step towards the optimization and modernization of the Tocosh production process, with the perspective of improving the quality and efficiency of this ancient method of food preservation.

articleTitle: Visualization Studies on Drying Patterns of Hydrogel Droplets
abstract: The phenomenon of droplet dynamics is widely seen in both natural and industrial contexts, including but not limited to spray painting, fuel injection, printing industries, and forensics. However, a deeper understanding of the governing factors is necessary in order to comprehend the various characteristics displayed by droplets in different applications. In the context of bio-applications, the natural drying process is distinguished by the physiochemical parameters of the fluid, including density, viscosity, and the presence of additives. The relationship between viscosity and applied shear rate, as well as surface properties, is particularly noteworthy in the context of complicated fluids. This study used two distinct additives, namely CaSo4 and Xanthan gum, to investigate the wetting and drying mechanisms of multicomponent fluids. The earlier is a simple bi-component solution that results in the formation of amorphous powder. In contrast, the Xanthan gum-based complex fluids exhibit shear-thinning behaviour and display distinct drying patterns. The drying patterns are found to be influenced by Marangoni effects, which arise as a consequence of mass transfer. The experimental findings indicate that the drying patterns, ranging from the formation of a coffee ring pattern to complete wetting, are influenced by the composition of the solution. Furthermore, rheological studies are necessary to understand the response features of additives in the drying behaviour of shear-thinning fluids.

articleTitle: Mechatronic System for the Detection and Monitoring of Arterial Hypertension: An Innovative Tool in Health Care
abstract: High blood pressure (HBP) is a globally significant health condition that affects a large number of people worldwide. This study presents an innovative approach for the early detection and continuous monitoring of HT using a mechatronic methodology. The guidelines of the Association of German Engineers (VDI-2206) were selected as the framework for the development of the system. The proposed device consists of a customised garment, such as a polo shirt, equipped with pulse, temperature and position sensors strategically placed on the wearer's body. The collected data is transmitted in real time through an electronic circuit controlled by an Arduino Uno to a centralised database. This data is accessible by medical professionals for analysis. The results obtained show the effectiveness of this approach in monitoring ETS, including the accurate measurement of heart rate and body temperature, as well as the identification of the user's position. This provides a comprehensive view of the patient's health and enables early detection of potential cardiac problems. In addition, a significant reduction in physician workload is observed by automating part of the monitoring process.

articleTitle: Convective Heat Transfer Enhancement Using Flow Divider Type Insert
abstract: Convective heat transfer enrichment represents an efficient technology for improving the performance of shell and tube heat exchangers. This technology finds application in various industrial sectors, including process industries, thermal power plants, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems, refrigeration systems, and automobile radiators. Techniques of Heat transfer enrichment encompass various methods used to improve the amount of heat transfer without compromising overall performance. These techniques are categorized as active, passive, and compound methods. The primary objective of this study is to investigate passive techniques for enhancing heat transfer. In this research, we employ a Flow Divider-type insert to boost heat transfer efficiency. Passive inserts disrupt the boundary layer, significantly enhancing heat transfer. These inserts transform laminar flow into turbulent flow. For this project, non-metallic inserts are utilized with air as the working medium, and various performance parameters are examined. While the insert improves the heat transfer rate, it also necessitates an increase in pumping power. Therefore, it is crucial to identify an insert that enhances the heat transfer rate with minimal additional pumping power. To assess this performance, we introduce an essential parameter known as the overall enhancement factor. This factor is the ratio of Nu/N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> to f/f0, and it should be maximized for optimal performance. In this experiment, the insert measures 25mm × 25mm and is 3mm thick, composed of carbon fiber material. The findings reveal that as Reynolds number increases, the Nusselt number increases while the friction factor decreases. It is also observed that the maximum heat transfer occurs at the maximum Reynolds number (22392), reaching 113.9094 W, while the minimum heat transfer (58.94 W) is observed at the minimum Reynolds number (11404). The highest friction factor (0.339458) is observed at a Reynolds number of 11252.78, while the lowest friction factor (0.055317) is noted at a Reynolds number of 19990.2457. These results underscore the importance of optimizing Reynolds numbers to achieve the desired heat transfer and pumping power balance.

articleTitle: A Framework for Generalization Error Evaluation in Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: Deep learning has introduced various paradigms in the healthcare industry. Deep Convolutional Neural Network models assist doctors in diagnosis, surgery, and other areas. Incidences of breast tumors are growing at a frightening pace. Thus, it is necessary to diagnose it so that the mortality count can be decreased. Generalizability defines how well the model performs on unseen data. When capturing mammograms different types of noise get added to the images. Noise may significantly diminish classification ability and make class separation more difficult. Thus, analyzing the model's generalization on noisy or unseen data is very important. This paper proposes an approach for analyzing generalization errors in Deep Convolutional Neural Networks by inducting noises such as Gaussian, Salt and pepper, and Speckle. We have utilized the CBIS-DDSM dataset. Three prominent deep neural network models- Inception v3, Dense Net 201, and EfficientNetB4- are fine-tuned to assess the model's efficiency on noisy data. Results proved that the DenseNet201 has minimum Generalization errors i.e. 0.12 and performs pretty well on noisy data with a minimum loss rate. On the other hand, maximum distortion is caused by Speckle Noise in Inceptionv3 and Efficient NetB4 leading to a considerable drop in accuracy. Inception v3 has the highest Generalization Error i.e. 0.61 and thus exhibits minimum generalization capability.

articleTitle: Emerging Trends of Digital Manufacturing in Bioimplants
abstract: Industry 4.0 has seen a significant shift in the manufacturing of metallic biomaterials, which are used to manufacture devices and products for biomedical sector applications, owing to the emergence of digital manufacturing technologies like 3D printing. Compared to conventional fabrication techniques, 3D printing techniques allow the fabrication of metallic materials that are extremely specific and inexpensive. In this context, this paper focuses on the design, manufacturing, and analysis of SS316L powder stents using Selective Laser Melting (SLM). However, the stent design and its manufacturing process viability were examined using Design for Additive Manufacturing (DFAM) tools such as CREO, Materialize Magics, and EOSTATE software. Further, the laser power and scan speed were selected as SLM input parameters, and their results were evaluated in terms of surface roughness parameters, surface topography, and geometrical features. Findings indicated that the obtained values of Ra 0.484 μm, Rq 0.560 μm, Rt 2.789 μm, and Rz 1.98 μm were within an acceptable range. SEM analysis of the resulting surface topography supported these findings. The overall study shows that Industry 4.0 digital techniques, like SLM, are an emerging approach to manufacturing bio-implants.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Solar Powered Fully Automatic Biodegradable Waste Sorter and Composter
abstract: India is well known for its population and then obviously, the side effects of increasing population. One of the major side effects of the increasing population is kitchen waste creation from individual homes or hotels. The major concern is regarding the inclusion of non-degradable waste in the overall waste created. The researchers contributed a lot to define the categories of waste, but segregation of waste is a trending and vital issue now. Not only in India but in all developing countries, more emphasis has been done on awareness of separating degradable waste from non-degradable ones and this motivates an engineer to design a machine/technology which will sort degradable waste from the non-degradable one. The waste sorter is designed to identify the type of waste based on the image processing technique and then sort it into two containers named green waste and non-degradable waste. In this work, a robotic arm has been designed which operates based on the instruction given by the controller. The controller takes input from a high resolution camera. The system developed can identify the type of waste based on the percentage of degradable waste included in one set of identification. The percentage level of degradable waste can be set manually as per the user's demand. The waste so sorted will be called degradable waste and can be used for several applications like compost. The system has been designed to operate completely on Solar Energy and hence charge controllers and battery systems are employed in it. This makes this machine as a form of green technology that can be placed anywhere in outside places and waste can be placed in its containers to get sorted. This model will certainly be helpful in municipal corporations where sorting of waste is the biggest headache. The sorted biodegradable waste is provided to the green dustbin and hence to the composter where the temperature and oxidation will be monitored effectively to create compost from the waste sorted. This compost will certainly be useful for agriculture fertilizer at no cost and with no pollution.

articleTitle: Classification of Mammographic Images using Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: The Breast Cancer death rate is increasing rapidly. Given the decrease in the death rate, the detection of tumors in the early stages becomes crucial. Mammography is a widespread screening technique. In this research, we propose a computer-aided detection (CAD) system using Deep learning to classify mammographic images into benign and malignant. Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models have been trained and tested with an online dataset. A public mammogram dataset called King Abdulaziz University Breast Cancer Mammogram Dataset (KAU-BCMD) from Kaggle is employed in our research. Experimentation has been done with Inception- V3,DenseNet-201, AlexNet, and VGG-19 CNN models. Inception-V3 CNN model has achieved a classification accuracy of89.75<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, Sensitivity of 84.3%, and Specificity of 91.19%, which is higher than that achieved by other CNN models.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Potential of Net Positive Energy and Carbon Houses: A Melbourne based Case Study
abstract: The building sector is responsible for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$36{{\% }}$</tex> of total energy consumption and one-third of the energy related greenhouse gas emissions around the world. There is an urgent need to reduce energy consumption and emissions from this sector. Previous studies investigated various ways to reduce operational carbon emissions by constructing net zero energy and emissions buildings. Nonetheless, reducing and offsetting embodied carbon emissions is still a challenge. This research investigated the potential of a Net Positive House to offset its embodied and operational carbon emission through two real world case studies. Net Positive Houses produce more energy than they consume, offering the potential to offset carbon emissions. The results revealed that the operation of these Net Positive Houses produced on average 6.6 times and 4.2 times more energy than they consumed over a full year. Net Positive Houses have the potential to not only achieve carbon neutrality in their operational phase, but also generate carbon credits for offsetting other carbon emissions. The two case study houses can offset their embodied carbon within approximately 3 years and 4.5 years depending on the occupants behavior. The battery storage was found to be more effective in terms of energy, cost and emissions savings for houses with higher energy consumption. These finding suggests that Net Positive Houses can play a crucial role in mitigating carbon emissions and advancing sustainability goals.

articleTitle: Traffic Signal Detection and Recognition from Real-Scenes Using YOLO
abstract: This research aims to create a robust system for detecting traffic lights using computer vision techniques. The proposed method uses image processing techniques and deep learning algorithms to detect and recognize traffic lights in real-time. Transfer learning is used to fine-tune a deep neural network model using a comprehensive dataset of annotated traffic light images. The trained model uses cutting-edge object detection algorithms to locate and identify traffic lights within input frames. Picture handling methods are then applied to refine the recognition results and dispose of bogus up-sides. The framework consolidates worldly examination to follow traffic signals across outlines, guaranteeing solid acknowledgment even in testing situations. Execution assessment utilizing genuine world datasets exhibits the framework's exactness, effectiveness, and potential for improving street well-being and keen transportation frameworks. Autonomous driving, traffic monitoring, and smart city infrastructure can all benefit from this research contribution to computer vision. The newly developed system for detecting traffic lights has the potential to make transportation systems safer and more effective.

articleTitle: Hybrid Dual Axis Solar Tracking System with Thermoelectric Generator to Improve the Energy Efficiency
abstract: Renewable energy is becoming a more important energy source as we deal with issues including growing energy prices, environmental degradation, and global warming. Sunlight is a key source of renewable energy. This paper represents the hybrid Arduino based dual axis solar tracking system with thermoelectric generator (TEG). A major downside of photovoltaic systems is that they only effectively convert a small part of solar light into energy, resulting in significant heat loss. When compared to single photovoltaic systems, the combination of photovoltaic (PV) and thermoelectric generator technology offers an effective way to exploit solar waste heat in increasing energy output. The Seebeck effect enables TEG modules to directly transform surplus thermal energy into electrical energy. The output voltage of TEG module is proportional to the temperature difference between hot side and cold side. TEG is connected to the rare side of the solar panel to harness the waste heat of the panel. While the cold side of TEG is cooled by continuous flowing water or still water, which is employed as a heat sink to maintain the temperature difference required to generate electrical output. The final experimental finding provides indisputably proof that the proposed approach is more effective than stand-alone PV system and single axis solar tracking systems. This hybrid system increases the efficiency by 10 to 15% compared to fixed stand-alone PV system

articleTitle: Development of a Prototype Concept for Using 3D Concrete Printing in Pavement Construction
abstract: The use of 3D Concrete Printing (3DCP) in road construction or rehabilitation is an area which has not been researched in depth. This study presents a concept for using 3DCP to reinforce the base or subbase layer of pavement to improve performance and possibly extend the service life. A particle-bed printing technique known as Aggregate-bed printing is proposed to strengthen the base and subbase layers in selective locations to improve the overall performance. Laboratory scale soil-box was developed to construct the layers and plate load tests (PLT) were carried out to compare the performance of unreinforced and selectively reinforced pavement layers. The results suggest that concrete reinforcement increases the bearing capacity of the subbase layer by 10%. The road base and subbase generally experience pressure values less than 550 kPa as it is protected by a surface layer, and the deformation values at lower magnitude of applied pressure were reduced by 35% by concrete reinforcement.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Effect of Different Configurations of Semi Circular or Half Round Ribs on Heat Transfer Enhancement in a Rectangular Duct
abstract: This research study investigates the impact of various configurations of half round shaped ribs on thermal performance and frictional effects through a rectangular duct. The ribs were provided only on inner surface of the rectangular duct's bottom wall. Six distinct configurations of half round ribs varying from continuous to hybrid arrangement were used. The range of Reynolds number was kept between 13,500 and 34,800; while the ratio of rib pitch and height was kept constant as 8. The ratio of height of rib to hydraulic diameter of duct (also known as blockage ratio) was kept at 0.114. The results of experimental investigation showed that the Nusselt number ratio obtained was ranging from 1.36 to 2.74, while the friction factor ratio ranges from 1.70 to 4.51. The overall enhancement ratio for all configurations obtained ranges from 1.06 to 1.80 times that of plain duct. Among all rib configurations, the hybrid rib configuration shows superior ratio of Nusselt number and intermediate increase in ratio of friction factor as compared to all the other rib configurations. Hybrid rib configuration shows overall enhancement ratio values ranging from 1.45 to 1.80 times as compared to that of duct without ribs within the above specified Reynolds number. From this study, the results showed that the hybrid configuration of ribs shows superior overall enhancement ratio in thermal manner over the remaining tested rib configurations.

articleTitle: Chat Master Using DJANGO
abstract: Chat Master is a powerful web application built using Django, a Python-based web framework following the MVC architectural pattern. It enables real-time communication between users using WebSocket, allowing for instant messaging and real- time updates. The user-friendly interface is designed using Django's templating system, separating presentation logic from backend code. Customization options are available, allowing users to tailor the application to their specific needs. Automatic message scrolling and updates are implemented using JavaScript, interacting with WebSocket to dynamically refresh the user interface without requiring a full page reload. Additionally, Chat Master includes functionality for training chatbots, leveraging machine learning algorithms to improve responses based on user interactions. Django handles the backend logic for training and updating chatbot models, while the frontend interface enables users to interact with and provide feedback for the training process. Overall, Chat Master offers a customizable and feature- rich experience for real-time chat and chatbot management.

articleTitle: Bursting of an Emulsion Droplet During Combustion
abstract: For decades, researchers have been exploring alternative fuels to counter the pollution problem caused by burning of fossil fuels. Emulsified fuels have attracted interest in the attempt to replace pure diesel. Water-in-diesel emulsion (WIDE) fuel has shown potential to be used in CI engines because of its reduced emissions and improved net fuel efficiency due to micro-explosions and presence of water content. This paper studies the emulsion's stability and investigates micro-explosion phenomenon by burning a droplet of the emulsion. Sophisticated videography and audiography are deployed to perform in-depth temporal analysis throughout the combustion period of the WIDE droplet.

articleTitle: Characterization of AlSi10Cu2 Aluminium Alloy Manufactured by Centrifugal Casting Route
abstract: Experimental research has been carried out regarding the manufacturing of aluminum alloy foams using centrifugal casting method and analysis of the samples so prepared. The work is primarily focused on measurement of parameters of centrifugal method of foam manufacturing and to check the appropriateness of hydrides like TiH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and LiAlH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> as foaming agents. During the manufacturing process, AlSi10Cu2 aluminum alloy is melted at a temperature of 600°C and the release of hydrogen gas is observed for minimum 10% weight (concentration) of Lithium Aluminium Hydride foaming agent. The foaming agent LiAlH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> is used as an alternatives for the traditional TiH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> foaming agent with the aid of powder metallurgy route. Subsequent analysis of the foam so produced has been done by visual observation, microstructure observation, X-ray diffraction analysis and SEM image analysis. The SEM analysis of the samples indicates the suitability of the method for aluminium foam formation and the porosity generated using the present method is comparable with that generated using present methods of manufacturing.

articleTitle: Environmental Impact Assessment of Assisted Ventilation
abstract: Environmental impacts of products and services have become a critical factor globally, highlighting the need for sustainable practices to protect both human health and the planet. This research demonstrates a life cycle assessment (LCA) of patients in the intensive care unit (ICU) with assisted ventilation of a hospital, to examine the associated environmental impacts. This study conducts a cradle-to-grave LCA, using openLCA software, which focuses on the consumables employed in assisted ventilation, including the breathing circuit, breathing bag, gloves, face mask, electricity consumption, and oxygen usage. The consumables used in assisted ventilation were listed from Dhaka Medical Hospital, Dhaka, Bangladesh, while material input data were gathered from relevant previous literature and public databases. The results indicate that electricity consumption and oxygen usage have the most significant impact on environmental factors.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Coiled Spring Wound Compact Heat Exchanger
abstract: A compact heat exchanger performs better under the same conditions as a traditional heat exchanger with less size, weight, and cost. In this study, a compact heat exchanger is prepared by coiling a copper spring of 19 gauge on a circular copper tube. Due to this wounding of spring the inner wire of the spring will touch the tubes of heat exchanger which will disturb the viscous sub layer of the fluid flow and hence resistance to heat transfer will decrease. The outer wire of the spring will act as fins and hence surface area of compact heat exchanger will increase which results in increase in heat transfer. The entire assembly of copper spring attached to copper tube is inserted in a PVC pipe. The temperatures at the inlet and outlet of heat exchanger are measured with calibrated thermocouple. The pressure drop at the inlet outlet is also measured. It is observed that the effectiveness of compact heat exchanger is increased by 2.1 times while the overall heat transfer coefficient is increased by 2.69 times of regular heat exchanger.

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled Secure Image Upload and Retrieval Preservation
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has become very popular due to the rise of smart gadgets. This technology has made our daily lives much more convenient. However, when using cloud-based IoT devices to store and transfer large numbers of pho-tos, there can be significant delays in the network. To tackle this issue, edge computing has emerged as a solution. By up-loading photos to nearby edge servers, data owners can avoid the delays and enjoy faster processing times. These edge serv-ers can efficiently handle the large amount of visual data from IoT devices, reducing transmission time and bandwidth usage. To address this data uploading and photo search problem, we are developing a system that utilizes edge computing for in-termediate processing.

articleTitle: Neuro Fuzzy Controller Based Cruise Control of Electric Vehicle
abstract: currently, cruise controllers and cruise systems are given a lot of attention by the automotive industry since they are one of the most important factors that call for a precise controller that can keep up with technological advancement. Running vehicles have complicated and changeable motions. Due to this, the cruise control system (CCS) exhibits substantial non- linearity, making it difficult to employ a typical PID controller under all circumstances. An investigation of neural fuzzy logic controllers for an automotive cruise control system (ACCS) using a linearized model of the cruise system is presented in this work. The benefits of neural networks and fuzzy logics are combined using fuzzy membership function-based neural networks. Its quick training makes it suitable for online learning. The demonstration of how to control EV speed has been done using m-file and MATLAB/SIMULINK. According to the results, neuro fuzzy controller performance responds more favorably to overshoot and settling time. NFN combines the efficient calculation, neural network learning capability, and approximate reasoning decision-making of fuzzy logic. The Neuro fuzzy logic control technique is helpful to regulate the BLDC motor's speed. By adjusting the load torque and speed, the evaluation of the suggested method is assessed which performs remarkably well in both situations.

articleTitle: Review of feasibility of IoT Protocols for 5G Industrial & Mobile Applications
abstract: Wireless and Mobile technology is experiencing rapid growth in terms of technology advancements and also in subscribed users. This is due to the pathbreaking advantages to these technologies in terms of almost all the Quality of Service (QoS) Parameters in many applications in all fields of life. Internet of Things (IoT) is one such platform which is largely dependent on and driving the future advancements. With the roll out of 5G specifications and technology readiness it has become interesting to check its feasibility to particular and specific applications using IoT or Industrial IoT (IIoT). This largely depends on the underlying protocol used for the communication between devices. MQTT, CoAP, AMQP, XMPP, WAP, HTTP and DDS are some of the protocols which are reviewed in this study and a comparative analysis is presented for the benefit of the researchers and developers for the implementation.

articleTitle: Seasonal Rainfall Forecasting Using Wavelet Based Hybrid Models
abstract: Present study forecast the seasonal summer rainfall in two distinct Northern Territory (NT), Australia stations by employing modified hybrid algorithms with a single level of enhancement. These algorithms utilize observed various climate anomalies, including El Niño Southern Oscillation (ENSO), Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), Interdecadal Pacific Oscillation (IPO), and Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO), as input variables for prediction. In this study, we initially employed two well-known machine learning algorithms, namely Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and Auto-Regressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), as the foundational algorithms. Subsequently, we utilized wavelet transform (WT) as a preprocessing method. The combination of ANN and ARIMA with WT, referred to as W-ANN and W-ARIMA respectively, constituted the first-level hybrid algorithms, incorporating all these components. We employed three statistical metrics to assess and validate the predictive accuracy of these algorithms. The results indicate that W-ANN and W-ARIMA hybrid algorithms consistently exhibited the highest predictive accuracy for seasonal rainfall, surpassing the individual algorithms. Furthermore, it was observed that the choice of mother wavelet type influenced the prediction accuracy of the W-ANN algorithm, with W-ARIMA algorithms consistently achieving the highest predictive accuracy with the selected wavelet.

articleTitle: M-CARE: Crafting Beauty from Sanitary Waste
abstract: Menstrual hygiene is important but discarding sanitary waste results in significant environmental and health risks. Poor disposal methods increase the amount of non- biodegradable waste in landfills and endanger human health. This research paper introduces M-Care, a revolutionary program that uses a comprehensive system to integrate smart technology, community participation and waste upcycling to solve the urgent problem of sanitary waste management. The M-Care project is a key step towards sustainable management of menstrual hygiene and can have a significant impact on upcycling and waste. It aims to change waste management practices through awareness campaigns and community engagement, leading to a cleaner environment and better public health. This study provides a significant overview of the creation, use and impact of the M-Care system and highlights its potential as a prototype for environmentally friendly waste management strategies.

articleTitle: Computer Vision Approach for Outdoor Color Rating of Guava: Design and Implementation
abstract: Now a days farmers identifies the ripeness of the fruits by its colors and segregates it by manual judgment. This system is more person orientation and different person may judge it differentially. In the current paper computer-based vision technique is used to find solution to the current problem. Computer based technique is the attempt for achieving automatic and objective based technique developed for reducing the farmer's effort. Computer program to made to make it easier for fruit farmers to rate the color of their fruits. This program can also get rid of shiny spots on the fruits. We tested it in real fields with different lighting, and it worked well. This shows that we can use computers to give fair and accurate color ratings to fruits like guavas, right in the orchard, under natural sunlight. The test was performed on outdoor condition, the result found was satisfactory. We have involved some of the farmer also in the process. They were satisfied with the results. The process for the finding result is very easy and can be done by any illiterate farmer. The initial devices and cost required for the test is quite less. We have conducted test on the 100 samples and got very good results. We have done three set of readings for checking the reproducibility of the program. The test outcomes also indicated that the system's overall accuracy stood at 93%, and we gathered 100 measurements across three distinct outdoor lighting conditions to arrive at this conclusion. Accuracy of the system was 91.99% when Radial basis function. Accuracy of the system was 94% when Linear basis function. This initial research confirmed that it's both possible and practical to utilize computer vision technology for delivering precise ratings. of Guava color in an orchard environment.

articleTitle: Sustainable Machining Using Minimum Quantity Lubrication with Nano Fluid*
abstract: Modern workshops and manufacturing industries are searching the solutions regarding minimization of coolant in metal removing operations along with environmental and economic impact. To overcome the issue of less heat carrying capacity and disposal of coolant minimum quantity lubrication is a better solution. Therefore, hybrid nano fluids are the mixtures of base cutting fluid and nano particles improves lubricating properties, and heat carrying capacity of nano-cutting fluid. In the present work study nano-cutting fluid is prepared by adding 0.2 % MWCNT nano particles to the base cutting fluid. Comparative study of surface roughness, cutting temperature, during machining of AISI 4340 with dry, conventional cutting fluid and nano-cutting fluid is studied. Present research work shows, due to better lubrication, the corresponding temperature rise is reduced by 26% as compared to flood cooling system. From research work, it is also shown that during MQL turning of alloy steel AISI 4340 with nano fluid is an appropriate cutting fluid as compared to conventional cutting fluid. This study clearly reveals that the work piece surface roughness, cutting temperature are reduced by the using nano-cutting fluid compared to dry machining and machining with conventional cutting fluid.

articleTitle: Solar Energy Integration Using Grid Forming Inverter
abstract: In this paper present, a grid forming inverter (GFMI) scheme with photovoltaic (PV) solar system that maintains the grid voltage constant using voltage source inverter (VSI). Also, literature on Grid following inverter (GFI) with various techniques for controlling grid current. The GFMI used to control grid voltage and frequency at transient conditions. Now a days Inverter based resources (IBRs) frequently trends to extract a maximum amount of power at near to load. IBRs are connected to grid by using GFMI with different control techniques like phase locked loop (PLL), droop control, PWM techniques, voltage controllers etc. Sinusoidal pulse width modulation technique used for generation of switching signal for switches in the voltage source inverter and dq0 theory is used for generating reference signal in VSI. Simulink model of PV solar system connected to grid with various control techniques described and result gives constant voltage at output side of inverter when PV solar output power get reduced to 50% of its initial value and it maintain constant dc voltage of inverter and also maintain the frequency at output side of inverter. PV solar system generate maximum power by using maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithm.

articleTitle: Mobile Augmented Reality for Industrial Training
abstract: Augmented Reality (AR) includes convergence between virtual and reality aspects, registration tracking, and advances in human interaction with computers. This fact is used to develop a mobile-based training model for the Indian Railways Institute of Civil Engineering (IRICEN), Pune. The civil engineering trainees at IRICEN understand how a train engine works through theory and a physical model installed in the model room. Most of the assembly and how the parts work together are left to one's imagination. With the rise in Edu-tech, the objective here was to create an interactive environment for learning by incorporating technologies like AR and facilitating a much more realistic representation of real-life processes. The goal is achieved with the help of software such as Unity, Blender, and Vuforia. A 3D model given by IRICEN company is created using Blender and Unity is used to disassemble and rotate the model. The information about each part of the model is displayed on the screen for a better understanding of the concept. The “Mobile Application (App)” is developed so that the model is accessible via the “App” by scanning the image of the model. The 3D model can be scaled by pinch, transformed in position by dragging, rotated by twisting, and disassembled by the pressing buttons displayed on the User Interface (UI) of the mobile screen. Indeed, AR can make a positive impact on education as well as industrial training.

articleTitle: CAN-Driven Automation: Paving the Way for Vehicle Automation
abstract: Controller Area Network (CAN) protocol, originally designed for real-time, robust, and reliable communication within the automotive domain, has played pivotal role in the growth of autonomous vehicles and advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS). Its unique attributes, such as high-speed data transmission, fault tolerance, and scalability, have made it the backbone of vehicle communication networks. This paper highlights the fundamental principles of CAN protocol working, highlighting its suitability for enabling vehicle automation. It explores the evolution of CAN-based automation from basic functionalities. Vehicle automation prototype implementation based on CAN bus is discussed.

articleTitle: The Metaverse for Stroke Motor Rehabilitation*
abstract: Stroke is a critical illness that causes disabilities and fatalities. The current standard motor rehabilitation usually requires some residual movement of stroke patients, limiting participation. Movement imagination, known as motor imagery (MI), potentially expedites motor rehabilitation by activating the motor brain areas, which may facilitate neuroplasticity. MI is, however, a difficult ability that may deteriorate over time. The Metaverse, a virtual reality (VR) social media platform, provides an immersive and interactive environment that allows stroke patients to experience the embodiment of their MI performance via their avatars. This paper provides a framework to design a Metaverse stroke motor rehabilitation program, outlining the essential elements required from the Metaverse and the challenges in implementing the Metaverse in stroke motor rehabilitation. Future research directions are identified that provide solutions and facilitate stroke recovery in motor functions through more advanced and innovative digital technologies suitable for vulnerable stroke patients.

articleTitle: Improving the Quality of Catimor Coffee: Design and Validation of a Dedicated Fermentation Machine
abstract: This study focused on the development of a coffee fermenting machine designed to enhance the organoleptic characteristics of the Catimor variety in the province of Chanchamayo, with the aim of increasing the value of Peruvian coffee in the international market. The implementation of this machine not only benefits local coffee farmers by improving their income, but also contributes to the consolidation of Peruvian coffee as one of the best in the world. The methodology adopted for the design process follows the guidelines of the German VDI 2221 standard, which allowed for an effective understanding of the steps required to complete the proposed design. Furthermore, the designed machine manages to reduce the fermentation time from approximately 24 to 12 hours, while improving the sensory properties of the coffee when tasted. The design approach was based on a thorough analysis of the needs of coffee farmers in Chanchamayo. This innovative project in fermentation technique was based on mimicking the fermentation process of the coati's digestive system, which allowed the addition of fruity aromas to the coffee beans. In the validation test, an increase of 5.25 points in organoleptic characteristics was achieved, thus meeting the objectives set. This progress will benefit the coffee-growing community of Chanchamayo by improving the yield in the cup, which in turn will increase the price of the product on the market.

articleTitle: Youth Unemployment Mitigation: Leveraging Machine Learning and Exploratory Data Analysis for Evidence-Driven Strategies
abstract: Youth unemployment represents an urgent global socioeconomic challenge. This study combines machine learning and exploratory data analysis to understand and solve this problem comprehensively. Traditional approaches often rely on qualitative assessments and historical data requiring a data-driven transition to more effective solutions. Our approach integrates machine learning algorithms and Exploratory Data Analysis techniques to analyze diverse data sets, identify influencing factors, and recommend targeted interventions. The analysis process includes data collection, preprocessing, feature selection, machine learning modeling, and Exploratory Data Analysis techniques to understand the dynamics of the Better understanding unemployment among young people. Preliminary results reveal precise predictive patterns and previously unrecognized relationships, providing evidence-based solutions to inform policy and support the economic well-being of younger generations. Further research and validation are needed to increase applicability.

articleTitle: Building Information Modelling for Constructability and Asset Management of Large Rail Infrastructure
abstract: In recent years there has been an increase in demand for large infrastructure projects such as railway. Railway projects are complex in nature involving multiple stakeholders, varied deliverables, and significant costs. Traditional methods for construction involve communication through 2D drawings. These are difficult to interpret and result in miscommunication and errors which lead to increased cost and delays. Building information modelling (BIM) has been seen as an approach to create a database to host all information (e.g.: 3D models, schedules, cost), however, extensively implemented in large infrastructures such as railways is lacking. Further, a key challenge that railway construction faces is understanding the constructability of the project prior to finalizing the schedule. The research presented a novel BIM implementation in large infrastructure (railway) and assessment of constructability studies. These included collision detection, site layout planning, asset management and quantity take-off were conducted. Overall, these constructability studies demonstrated potential time and cost savings.

articleTitle: Bridging the Semantic Gap:Automated SQL Query Generation from Natural Language
abstract: Natural language processing and computer science researchers are exploring the conversion of natural language queries into SQL to bridge the gap between humans and machines. This process involves parsing the query, determining the database schema, creating a corresponding SQL query, and running the SQL query against the database. Researchers have explored methods like rule-based systems, machine learning algorithms, and neural networks. The conversion has several uses, including making databases more accessible, enabling non-technical users to extract information, and combining Natural Language Processing (NLP) with other disciplines like data analytics and business intelligence. The first stage involves using NLP approaches like tokenization, part-of-speech tagging, and named entity recognition to deconstruct the query into its components. The second stage involves translating the query's keywords into relevant SQL keywords and clauses. This technology has real-world applications in business intelligence, data analytics, and customer service, reducing the need for specialized training and technical competence.

articleTitle: Harnessing Digital Twins for Fostering City-Scale Entrepreneurial Ecosystems: Extending a Case Study of Melbourne
abstract: This article considers the utility of deploying a digital twin (DT) as a third way for governments to support local entrepreneurial ecosystems. We investigate the function of a digital twin in coordinating, predicting, and enabling a multi-stakeholder ubiquitous knowledge system to foster innovation inside the city through a city-specific case study. Conceptually, we take an ecosystem approach that underlines the interconnectedness of human and non-human actors and agencies within this system and is based on the idea of complex adaptive systems. We use this method to comprehend the linked difficulties the entrepreneurial ecosystem faces in Melbourne, the state capital of Victoria, Australia. We investigate the function of an entrepreneurial ecosystem digital twin (EEDT) in addressing the issues of wealth recycling and talent attraction that are highlighted in this case study. To provide specificity on how this achieved, we articulate the architecture of an EEDT using a multilayered approach that distinguishes between actions ranging from data aggregation to policy governance. The EEDT architecture described incorporates attributes of modularity, scalability, and a high degree of customisability, making it adaptable to different entrepreneurial ecosystems with varying needs and characteristics. Finally, we emphasise that an EEDT is not trouble-free and that concerns about the inevitable data politics are raised by its substantial dependence on automation and data.

articleTitle: Ergonomic Factors Impacting Industrial Operator Performance, Productivity, and Musculoskeletal Health
abstract: This paper investigates the intricate relationship between workplace factors and their influence on the occurrence of Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders (WMSDs). It delves into the factors affecting industry operators' performance, emphasizing the role of organizational, ergonomic, and individual factors as triggering elements. To quantitatively assess these factors' contributions to a person's work productivity, a novel grid model is proposed, enabling a structured evaluation. The study involved a cohort of ten actively participated in the study. Participants provided insights into workplace conditions significantly affecting WMSDs through a meticulously designed questionnaire. The mathematical model presented here adopts a systematic and analytical approach, employing algebraic equations to represent both hyperbolic and linear relations. This model establishes a structured framework for the assessment and optimization of workplace conditions, ultimately aiming to reduce the incidence of WMSDs. Parametric studies were conducted to evaluate the model's effectiveness, facilitating the prediction of different factors' impacts on the performance index linked to WMSD reduction. Results indicate that ergonomic factors affected 60% of the participants’ performance. Similarly, individual factors affected 20% and organisational factors affected 50% of the participant's performance. This paper sheds light on the dynamic interplay of these factors, offering valuable insights for the prevention of WMSDs in various occupational settings.

articleTitle: Next Sequence Number Prediction in Natural Languages using Deep Learning
abstract: Natural languages Generation mainly focus on generating human interpretable languages This study suggests an innovative method to guess the following sequence number and user's keystrokes can be minimized by anticipating the subsequent sequence. For the job of guessing the next number, two deep learning techniques Long Short Term Memory and Bi-LSTM (Bi-directional-LSTM) have been investigated. This method perhaps utilized with a range of NLG(Natural Language Generation) tasks, including sentence and auto completion. A key problem in many fields, from time series analysis to natural language processing, is the prediction of sequential data. LSTM setups have shown to be successful at identifying patterns in such data and modeling sequence dependencies.  Paper will investigate the use of LSTM networks for forecasting future numerical sequences. The experiment with various sequence lengths, network designs, and hyper parameters to show the efficacy of our method. The predictive power of the LSTM model with that of standard techniques like moving averages and autoregressive algorithms. This method also examine the model's sensitivity to noisy or irregular data as well as its ability to generalize to various kinds of numerical sequences.

articleTitle: Detection of Broiler Behaviors Through a Wearable Sensor System and Machine Learning Methods
abstract: The wellbeing of broiler chickens is an increasing concern in society. This has a direct bearing on the standard of animal farmed products and the overall health of those who eat them. Importantly, taking good care of animals has a big impact on helping broilers grow healthy. This also leads to fewer diseases and makes the quality and amount of bird products better. This study's primary objective is to categorize different broiler behaviors since these responses are important welfare markers. This endeavor is achieved through the meticulous analysis of data acquired from wearable accelerometers, utilizing an array of machine learning models, namely Discriminant Analysis (DA), Decision Trees (DT), Naïve Bayes (NB), K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Ensemble Classifiers. The Quadratic-SVM study showed the best performance of 84.8% and an F-measure of 86.1% overall, while the Coarse Gaussian-SVM analysis showed the lowest performance of 15.0% and an F-measure of 15.7 %. The results show our method's potential for accurately determining specific broiler behaviors, making it helpful for implementation in the future.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Machine Learning Techniques for Malaria Diagnosis from Blood Samples
abstract: This study paper provides an overview of the use of machine learning techniques for malaria diagnosis. The article looks at a variety of machine learning algorithms, such as supervised and unsupervised learning, deep learning techniques, and hybrid approaches, and how they might be used to diagnose malaria. In addition, widely used data sets and preprocessing methods for detecting malaria are discussed, as well as evaluation metrics for determining how well machine learning models work. The paper highlights how machine learning might improve patient outcomes and change the diagnosis of malaria, particularly in areas with limited resources. The paper concludes with a summary of key findings and contributions, limitations, and open research questions for future work.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Smart Head-Motion Controlled Wheelchair
abstract: The everyday challenges faced by those who are immobile due to congenital defects, arthritis, high blood pres-sure, age, or stroke are significant. Addressing this issue, we propose the design of an autonomous mobility system tailored to this specific demographic. This innovative system not only governs the movement of a wheelchair but also incorporates obstacle-detection capabilities. Our solution revolves around an automatic head-movement-controlled wheelchair, enabling uni-directional navigation through intuitive head gestures (forward, backward, left, and right). It seamlessly halts movement when the user ceases head motions. This system comprises two pivotal components: the transmitting unit and the receiving unit. Changes in head orientation are detected by a gyro sensor in the transmitting unit, which then uses ESP32 and HTTP machine-to-machine communication to send signals. These signals are captured by the receiving unit with the aid of another ESP32. The ESP32 performs the functions of a microcontroller and a transceiver in both the transmit and receive units. Subsequently, DC motors with the help of L298 interpret these commands, orchestrating precise wheelchair movements. The integration of ultrasonic sensors enhances safety by enabling obstacle detection. Combining data from the gyro sensor and ultrasonic sensors, the system intelligently guides the wheelchair. When obstacles are detected ahead, either to the left or to the right, the system ensures immobility until a clear path is available. The user can change direction by simply moving their head backward and subsequently instructing movement in the desired direction. There is also a wireless control system, so if a wheelchair patient's family member wants to, they can easily control the wheelchair through our mobile app or our website. It is also possible to track the wheelchair's realtime location in our app and on our website using GPS, GSM, and IoT technologies. A crash alert is also present. If the patient falls out of the wheelchair, a beeping buzzer on the wheelchair will sound, and the patient's family members will receive a call and an SMS. Through the mobile app and website, the alert can be followed. Our primary objectives are simplicity and efficiency. The suggested system's quick response times and low cost will be advantageous to people with serious mobility issues.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Privacy Preservation and Security in Cloud Databases using Blockchain Technology
abstract: Cloud databases provide organizations with scalable and flexible data storage and management capabilities. However, concerns around data privacy and security in cloud environments remain a major barrier to adoption. This paper explores how blockchain technology can be applied to enhance privacy preservation and security for cloud databases. A review of cloud database architectures, privacy and security risks, and existing solutions is provided. The unique capabilities of blockchain to enable tamper-proof, decentralized data sharing are discussed. A proposed blockchain framework for securing cloud databases is presented, including system components and workflow. Central elements include encryption, access control, auditing, and smart contracts enabled by blockchain and cryptographic techniques. Benefits of the blockchain approach such as immutable audit logs, prevention of unauthorized data modification, and cryptographic privacy are highlighted. Implementation considerations including performance, cost, and deployment tradeoffs are analyzed. Overall, blockchain shows strong potential to mitigate cloud database privacy and security concerns through its decentralized trust model, although further research and development is needed to address scalability and efficiency challenges. The paper provides comprehensive analysis of the application of blockchain for enhanced cloud database security to benefit both academic researchers and industry practitioners.

articleTitle: Effective Food Demand Forecasting Using Machine Learning Algorithms
abstract: Demand forecasting is a fundamental strategy used by companies to predict future demand for their goods and services based on an examination of historical demand in light of the present state of the market. The food business places a lot of importance on this process. Accurate forecasting is necessary in the food business since perishables have a short shelf life and cause operating costs to rise. The goal of this project is to use historical data to predict weekly grocery shipments for a given business. The business intends to create a solid forecasting model that can precisely estimate future demand for food delivery by examining historical demand patterns, industry trends, and other pertinent aspects. We can use this information to streamline operations, plan inventory, and allocate resources efficiently. Accurate demand forecasting has many benefits for food delivery and restaurant businesses. First, we can optimize work distribution and schedule the right number of employees during peak demand periods, while avoiding unnecessary spending during low-peak periods. Second, food waste can be minimized by enabling businesses to source and stock the right amount of ingredients and perishables. This reduces the risk of corruption and allows for better cost control. Finally, accurate demand forecasting improves overall customer satisfaction by ensuring on-time delivery and menu item availability, leading to increased customer loyalty and positive reviews. Historical data from company operations is used to develop effective demand forecasting models. By accurately predicting future demand, businesses can adjust pricing and advertising strategies to maximize sales and profits. For instance, if the system forecasts strong demand for a specific product during a specific season, the business can raise the product's price to improve profits during that time.

articleTitle: A Review On: Automated Surveillance System
abstract: Research involving human surveillance is crucial for addressing safety concerns. The growing need for safety in a variety of settings has sparked a flurry of activity in the field of surveillance technology research and development in recent years. Most current surveillance systems rely on monocular cameras, which are limited in their ability to offer three-dimensional depth information for person detection and tracking due to their fixed field of view. The growing need for safety in public places like schools, hospitals, airports, and malls has made automated video surveillance systems a hot topic of study in recent years. Detecting an object, then classifying it so that it may be tracked later, has become a standard feature of video surveillance. Target identification in successive video frames can be achieved using object tracking, although detecting an item might be challenging due to factors such as lighting changes, ambient factors, pose changes, occlusion, motion blur, and so on. Night vision detection is a challenging procedure that is nonetheless crucial in the battle against crime, public safety, and the efficient management of day-to-day labour. One difficult issue in the ever-changing world of video surveillance is the detection of abandoned objects in public areas. The suggested method employs background reduction and morphological filtering to recognize unattended items in a live setting. The discovery of the abandoned suspicious object and the timely notification of the appropriate authority is our primary objective.

articleTitle: Weed Classification for Smart farming in Field Crops: A Machine Learning Evaluation
abstract: For any domain, the application of Machine Learning (ML) remains a complicated process that requires experimentation with multiple techniques to find the effective ML model. This process could easily be compromised due to its complexity. In more complicated applications that involve big data and deep learning, it becomes even more important to thoroughly explore the behavior of ML to save time and resources for future applications. This paper explores the application of ML to detect and classify weeds. This is critical as weeds can potentially cause significant financial losses to the agricultural industry. We analyze and compare the performance of 15 ML models for classifying weed types using the widely used ResNet50 and VGG16 pre-trained convolutional neural networks as feature selectors on standard datasets. We conduct two different applications: 1) individual ML algorithms, and 2) stacked generalization which stacks RandomForest, GradientBoosting and SVM, classifying further results with Logistic Regression. For individual ML applications, the summarized results show that RidgeClassifier performed the best on ResNet50 and VGG16, while LinearSVC and LogisticRegression also performed well on both models. However, some models, such as the KNeighborsClassifier and GaussianNB, showed poor performance on both models. The stack algorithm gave the best accuracy of 96.3% with VGG16. Furthermore, the time taken for each model varied greatly, with some models much faster than others. Our detailed results provide guidance regarding the selection of ML models and techniques for weed classification tasks while using pre-trained VGG16 and ResNet50 feature selectors.

articleTitle: Performance Optimisation of Regression-Based Machine Learning Models to Predict Mineral Land Prices for Tokenization
abstract: The tokenization of in-ground mineral land involves the digital conversion of physical mineral assets by issuing security tokens registered on a blockchain. This transformative approach offers the potential to fractionalize mineral land ownership, enhancing market liquidity, accessibility, and transparency. However, the accuracy of mineral land price prediction is paramount for its success. Historically, traditional methods such as geostatistical techniques, geometric modelling, kriging, and Inverse Distance Weighting were employed for price prediction. Yet, geological complexities and unpredictable external factors have posed formidable challenges. Hence, it is critical that mining companies have the capability to accurately predict the mineral land price to evaluate the feasibility of their mining operations and provide a fair market valuation to critical stakeholders. To address these challenges, this paper empirically evaluates three machine learning algorithms: multiple linear regression, gradient boosting models, and deep neural network models (DNN) for mineral land price prediction in the context of tokenization. Leveraging a dataset from a Western Australian mineral deposit with Gold, Iron, and Nickel commodities across 45 mine sites, the results demonstrate that the DNN approach, when fine-tuned with the Keras Tuner method, outperforms other models, yielding an optimized Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 5154.42.

articleTitle: Extracting Key Value Streams Using Process Mining and Machine Learning
abstract: In the past decade, the complexity of production systems has grown exponentially. Manufacturing companies are under the influence of social, economic, and political trends that urge them to accelerate product development timelines while simultaneously achieving greater flexibility and resource efficiency. Amid these challenges, manufacturing companies commonly grapple with the task of defining key value streams within their production processes. This challenge is especially relevant for high-variety, low-volume businesses where value streams may include a high number of products and components. The identification of these key value streams offers a pathway to improve decision-making, shedding light on the primary sources of complexity that impede operational efficiency. Central to this endeavour is a comprehensive grasp of production flows. In the context of Industry 4.0, the expanded accessibility of data sourced from factory operations opens doors to novel prospects, facilitating a more profound understanding of production flows. Following the long-standing principles of Production Flow Analysis, which have played a pivotal role in defining value streams over the years, we present an approach for discerning these value streams by harnessing production data through process mining and machine learning techniques.
